close_reason: Fixed in 331a8ee: ChatPresenceEvent.presence is now Presence, in parity with ChatContact and PresenceStatus. Forward-compat Other(_) preserves unknown wire values byte-equivalently. Parallel ChannelPermission.target_type defect tracked at bd:JMAP-pbqe.
description:
Trigger: a contributor (or future-you in 12 months) writes server code that matches on ChatContact.presence against the Presence enum and then tries to do the same for an incoming ChatPresenceEvent.

Bad behavior: ChatPresenceEvent.presence is typed as String (crate-jmap-chat-types/src/ephemeral.rs:74), while the parallel field on ChatContact (contact.rs:67-68) is Option<Presence>, and on PresenceStatus (presence.rs:42) is Presence — the typed enum with 'online' / 'away' / 'busy' / 'invisible' / 'offline' / Other(String) forward-compat.

The mismatch matters for two reasons:
1. WebSocket ephemeral handlers cannot exhaustively dispatch on the enum and instead must string-match — including reimplementing the wire vocabulary inline. That's the exact pattern that breaks when impl_string_enum! gains a new variant; both sites have to be updated and there is no compile-time tripwire forcing the second update.
2. It quietly violates the canonical-template rule. The workspace AGENTS.md anoints jmap-chat-types as canonical for the JMAP Chat wire format, and this is a presence value on the wire — it should use the Presence enum like every other use of the same value.

Fix: change ChatPresenceEvent.presence to Presence (the typed enum). It is non-breaking deserialize-wise because Presence already has an Other(String) forward-compat arm, and Presence already round-trips the wire form. The break is on the Rust struct API, but ChatPresenceEvent is #[non_exhaustive] and the crate has not yet shipped a 1.0, so this is a 0.x-version-bump-acceptable change.

Same issue, smaller scale, on ChannelPermission.target_type (chat.rs:59) — String where the spec enumerates 'role' / 'user'. Worth fixing in the same sweep but lower priority because the consumer surface is smaller.
title: ChatPresenceEvent.presence is String; everywhere else it is the Presence enum
